business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confédération suisse / Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft / Confederazione Svizzera)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil law (continental European / Swiss codal tradition; federal statutes such as the Swiss Code of Obligations, the Swiss Civil Code, and specialized federal acts; cantonal implementing regulations; limited case law influence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1982, in force 1986)
Switzerland–United States Treaty on Friendship, Commerce and Navigation (1850, as applicable)
Free Trade Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the European Economic Community (1972)
Over 90 Double Taxation Agreements (DTAAs) including with Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the United States, and China
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention, 1958)
Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID, 1968)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997; Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO, SR 955.01); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), articles 697j–697m (Beneficial Owners Register) and the Beneficial Owners Ordinance (SR 221.214), in force since 1 July 2023; Federal Act on Economic Sanctions (Embargo Act, SR 946.203); Federal Act on the International Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI Act, SR 653.1).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority / civil registry in country of origin of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (party to the 1961 Hague Convention; consular legalization if apostille unavailable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Incumbency for any corporate shareholder or intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the country of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public at the principal place of business of the appointing party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming business relationship and source of wealth of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or financial institution maintaining the UBO relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature verification plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration of beneficial ownership (UBO declaration) executed before a Swiss notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public in the canton of registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization under Swiss law; no apostille required for domestic document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on every natural person holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of share capital or voting rights, or exercising control by other means. Screening must cover the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Swiss SECO sanctions measures (Embargo Act), EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (as Swiss banking best practice), and national PEP databases, with continuous negative-news monitoring and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth documentation. Financial intermediaries must retain identification and transaction records for 10 years under AMLA and file suspicious transaction reports with MROS (Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal Commercial Register (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce / Registro di commercio), operated by cantonal Commercial Register Offices; official online portal: Zefix (www.zefix.ch); publication organ: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC, www.shab.ch).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be entered in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, or Italian; Romansh only in designated cantons) and in Latin script (Art. 950 Swiss Code of Obligations). The name must contain the legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' and may be a free word, a personal name, or a fancy name; it must not mislead, conflict with public order or morality, or unlawfully infringe third-party rights. Foreign-language or transliterated elements are permitted only to the extent they are not misleading and are rendered in Latin script.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Holding (requires actual holding-company activity and evidence of control over subsidiaries)
Swiss / Schweizer / Helvetia / Helvétique (requires Federal Council authorization under SR 232.11)
Eidgenössisch / Federal / Confederation (implies official state authority)
International / World / Global (requires objectively demonstrated international scope)
AG / SA suffix only; no foreign equivalent abbreviations without recognition
Names implying a public-law body, foundation, or state institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: There is no formal statutory name-reservation system in the Swiss Commercial Register; the notary conducts a preliminary availability check via Zefix, which de facto secures the proposed name for 30 days pending execution of the notarial deed. If the Commercial Register Office rejects the name, the notary will ordinarily file a corrected article within 7 days. Formal recourse: file a written objection with the cantonal Commercial Register Office within 10 days of service of the rejection; if dismissed, appeal to the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority (Kantonale Aufsichtsbehörde); final administrative appeal lies to the Federal Supervisory Commission for the Commercial Register (Eidgenössische Kommission für die Handelsregisterführung) within 10 days of service, attaching the rejection decision and stating legal grounds. Parallel refiling of a modified name is permitted without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for pure equity-holding SPVs: the registered office must be a real Swiss address in the municipality named in the articles of association (Art. 620 et seq. Swiss Code of Obligations). A licensed domiciliation provider may host the registered office, and this is standard for passive holding vehicles; however, a purely virtual office without any physical Swiss presence is not accepted by the Commercial Register. The domiciliation provider must be independent from the UBO and must comply with AMLA obligations if it acts as a financial intermediary.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; quantified annual risk is approximately 10–15% for a passive ISIC 6420 equity-holding SPV, increasing to 25–35% where the SPV holds crypto/fintech subsidiaries or maintains relationships with private banks. Unannounced inspections may be conducted by cantonal tax authorities, the Commercial Register Office, or criminal authorities investigating money laundering under Articles 305bis and 305ter of the Swiss Criminal Code.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht), Arts. 620–763; especially Arts. 626, 628, 634–635, 716b, 722 and 777a–777f; Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung); Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code (Part Five: Code of Obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office, coordinated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized incorporation deed (Errichtungsakt) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten/Statuts) and the formal application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Handelsregistereintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% (in all cases a minimum of CHF 50,000) must be fully paid up in cash or by contribution in kind before registration. For a pure equity holding SPV, contributions in kind are permitted for the subscription of subsidiary shares and must be evidenced by a capital payment confirmation from the Swiss bank or fiduciary holding the funds in an escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [Company Name] AG, Zurich. The sole shareholder subscribed all 1,000 bearer shares at the nominal value of CHF 100, each, fully covered by (i) cash and (ii) the in-kind contribution of the subsidiary shares. The Board resolves to adopt and file the Articles of Association; to adopt the registered office at [Street], Zurich; to appoint [Chair], [Secretary] and, where legally required, an independent auditor; and to authorize the Managing Director to open formation escrow account with [Bank] and to execute all Commercial Register filings without further consent, effective as of entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution and Authentication of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss public notary (Notariat/Office du notaire) in the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole founder must appear physically before the notary with the final draft Articles of Association. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the full subscription of the CHF 100,000 nominal capital, and the admissibility of any contribution in kind; the notary then minutes the incorporation deed, authenticates the Articles and delivers certified copies for registry use.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of the founder
Final draft of the Articles of Association (Statuten)
In-kind contribution report (Sacheinlageprüfungsbericht) if shares are subscribed against contributed subsidiary shares
Proof of the founder's civil capacity and, if applicable, corporate authorization
Certified copy of the power of attorney for any representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, the deed must be corrected and re-notarized; minor amendments may be executed by a supplementary notarial instrument (Nachtragsurkunde) and resubmitted within the same application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit and Confirmation of Minimum Paid-Up Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-regulated Swiss bank or licensed fiduciary institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the formation name, deposit at least CHF 50,000 representing the paid-up portion of the nominal capital, and contractually restrict the account so that funds are released only for the company's formation and initial operations. Obtain the bank's written Liberierungsbestätigung (confirmation of capital payment) signed by an authorized bank officer, which must be annexed to the registry application.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed or draft Articles
Beneficial ownership declaration (BO form)
KYC package including passport and proof of address of the ultimate beneficial owner
Signed escrow instruction letter designating the bank as escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On any compliance hold, provide supplementary proof of origin of funds and updated corporate chart; alternatively, replace the deposit with an irrevocable bank guarantee (Bankgarantie) issued for the benefit of the company in formation, acceptable to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with federal supervision by EHRA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal application for entry of the Aktiengesellschaft via the registered online platform or in writing at the competent cantonal office. The application must be signed by all directors with certified specimen signatures and accompanied by the prescribed annexes; the registry reviews legal capacity, permitted corporate purpose, capital rules and the identity of all signatories.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized incorporation deed
Articles of Association in two signed copies
List of the members of the Board of Directors with nationality and residence details
Specimen signatures (unterschriftsbeglaubigte) of all authorized signatories
Capital payment confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) from the Swiss bank
Consent of the auditor if a statutory audit is required
Application form (Anmeldung) with purpose restricted to ISIC 6420 passive holding activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a formal correction order (Verfügung), rectify the deficiencies within the stated deadline and resubmit; if the objection concerns the corporate purpose, adjust the Articles to exclude operational activities and refile; any adverse final decision may be appealed to the cantonal administrative court within 10 statutory days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entry into the Commercial Register and Publication in the Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office, with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the company acquires legal personality at the moment of entry. The registry publishes the corporate name, legal form, registered office, purpose, share capital, directors and binding signature modalities in the SHAB. The company must then download its extract (Handelsregisterauszug) which serves as official proof of existence.
required_dossiers: Extract from the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug)
Confirmation of publication in SHAB
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published entry contains errors or omissions, apply immediately for a rectification order at the Commercial Register Office; refusal may be appealed to the cantonal supervisory authority for commercial registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office (BFS) for UID allocation; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for VAT and withholding tax; cantonal tax administration for corporate income tax assessment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of Commercial Register entry, register the company with the federal UID central clearing system, apply for VAT registration if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year (voluntary registration is recommended for a holding SPV to claim GST on finance costs), and file the beneficial owner declaration for withholding tax purposes. Contact the cantonal tax administration for income tax and capital tax assessment procedures.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (recently issued)
UID registration form (eService of the FSO)
VAT registration form (MWST/IVA)
Beneficial ownership declaration (BO form) for withholding tax purposes
Copy of the Articles of Association and Board resolution on tax representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority fails to issue a UID or VAT number within the statutory period, submit a reminder and, if still delayed, apply for a declaratory ruling; late registration triggers interest but can be cured by filing the delayed form with a mitigating statement of good faith.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no operative industrial authority for a passive equity holding SPV; any future physical activity would fall under the Cantonal Office of Economy and Employment (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or commercial operating permit required; the passive holding of subsidiary shares and receipt of dividends falls outside the licensing scope of the cantonal commercial legislation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) with the cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no registration or full EIA required; the activity under ISIC 6420 is not listed in the EIA Regulation (UVPV) Annex because it creates no physical project, construction works or material emissive operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure financial holding activities. If a future registered office lease installs HVAC systems or a small server room, comply conditionally with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) Annex 2.2 discharge limits and the Ordinance on VOC Emissions (VOCV) thresholds for any coating or cleaning solvents; waste handling rules of the Ordinance on Waste Movements (VEVA) apply only if waste generators exceed 50 kg per year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety certification, structural load inspection or workplace occupancy clearance is mandatory for a mailbox-style registered office of a pure holding SPV without employees. If physical premises are eventually staffed, the company must obtain the cantonal fire department acceptance certificate (Feuerpolizeiliche Abnahme), comply with the Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz) on workplace conditions, and register employees with the compensation fund and the caisse de prévoyance before commencement of work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV), portal https://www.estv.admin.ch, responsible for VAT, federal withholding tax and stamp duties; cantonal tax administrations (Kantonale Steuerverwaltungen) assess federal, cantonal and communal direct taxes; the Uniform Business Identifier register is at https://www.uid.admin.ch and the commercial register portal at https://www.zefix.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Swiss Aktiengesellschaft: (1) notarise the articles of association and file incorporation with the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt), disclosing the ultimate beneficial owner; (2) after registration the Federal Statistical Office automatically allocates the UID (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx), which functions as the general tax identification number; (3) for VAT, submit the electronic registration to the FTA via the e-VAT portal or the UID/VAT registration form, stating the opening balance sheet date and the expected annual turnover; a foreign-resident business with no Swiss establishment must simultaneously appoint a Swiss VAT representative/agent for service of documents; (4) file the opening tax declaration with the competent cantonal tax administration for federal, cantonal and communal profit tax; total timeline approximately 7–14 business days after commercial register publication.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law has no US-style check-the-box election and an AG is not pass-through eligible; the relevant statutory elections are: (a) the participation deduction (Beteiligungsabzug, Art. 70 DBG and Art. 28 SHIG) for qualifying dividends and capital gains from participations of at least 10% or with an acquisition cost of at least CHF 1 million, the decisive relief for a pure equity holding SPV; (b) the VAT group election under Art. 11 MWSTG; (c) the option to waive the VAT registration threshold exemption; (d) binding advance tax rulings (Verbindliche Auskunft) from the cantonal/FTA authorities; (e) the transitional step-up facilities and notional interest deduction on new equity approved under the 2020 corporate tax reform; hybrid mismatch adjustments under Art. 61a DBG override elective outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA; MWSTG-LTVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A resident business is obliged to register for Swiss VAT when its worldwide annual turnover from taxable supplies exceeds CHF 100,000 (uniform threshold since 1 January 2018; CHF 150,000 for non-profit, cultural or sporting bodies); voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Non-resident businesses without a Swiss place of business supplying digital or electronic services to Swiss private consumers are registrable from the first franc, whereas qualifying B2B services are dealt with by the Swiss recipient under the reverse-charge procedure.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland imposes no continuous transaction controls, no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-mandated invoice stamping and no mandatory e-invoicing; invoices must nevertheless satisfy Art. 26 MWSTG (seller's name and UID, invoice date, description, consideration and VAT rate). The Swiss QR-bill and eBill are the standard structured invoicing/payment instruments, the electronic VAT return must be submitted through the FTA's e-VAT portal or certified XML interface, and the standardised ESTVAudit file must be produced during fiscal audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplied by a Swiss VAT-registered entity are zero-rated under Art. 23 MWSTG where the goods physically leave Switzerland and the export is proved by a Swiss customs export declaration (Ausfuhr- bzw. Exportzollanmeldung) with the corresponding customs release; services connected with exported goods (transport, handling, inspection, freight) qualify where performed directly for the exporter or for a foreign buyer. Dividend and capital-gain income received by a pure equity holding SPV is outside the scope of Swiss VAT (Leistung ohne Entgelt), so no output tax is charged; recharged management, financing or guarantee services are assessed under the place-of-supply rules and may be zero-rated, exempt, or subject to reverse charge for the Swiss recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (Exportzollanmeldung) with customs release/visa evidencing physical removal from Switzerland
Commercial invoice and sale or service contract establishing the foreign purchaser/recipient and delivery terms
International transport document (bill of lading, CMR waybill or air waybill) covering the whole export movement
Proof of receipt of the foreign payment (bank transfer confirmation such as SWIFT MT103 or other inward remittance evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: An inadequately substantiated export is retroactively reclassified as a domestic taxable supply: output VAT at 8.1% is clawed back with statutory default interest and corrected input VAT deductions are recovered from the exporter. Under Arts. 92 and 94 MWSTG, intentional evasion is sanctioned with a fine of up to four times the evaded tax and gross negligence with a fine of up to twice the evaded tax (ordinary negligence usually without fine); the assessment limitation extends to ten years in evasion cases, recurring false zero-rating can lead to loss of the right to use simplified accounting, and the FTA may publish final sanction decisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), assisted by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking and financial-market supervision under the National Bank Act and the Financial Market Supervision Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland applies full convertibility on both current and capital account under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments and the Swiss Debt Collection and Bankruptcy Law; there are no foreign-exchange restrictions on inward or outward remittances. Profit repatriation in the form of dividends is unrestricted from an FX perspective, but a 35% Swiss dividend withholding tax applies unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable double taxation treaty; the holding entity must therefore manage Swiss and foreign WHT recovery timelines.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement in Switzerland; no mandatory timeline or conversion ratio applies to export receipts. Export earnings may be retained in any convertible currency or freely sold back to CHF. The only relevant requirement is statistical/reporting in nature, as Swiss banks must report cross-border payment transactions to the Swiss National Bank when prescribed thresholds are met, according to the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF and multi-currency) and Escrow Sub-Account
Operational Account and Custody Account for Reserve Liquidity
Operational Current Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Current Account and Term Deposit
Private Banking Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI services are feasible only as a secondary payment channel, not as a primary treasury or settlement rail. A non-Swiss EMI holding only a e-money licence in a foreign jurisdiction cannot access Swiss SIC clearing or provide a native Swiss IBAN without additional authorisation; any such provider would be classified as a third-party intermediary and may trigger enhanced due diligence. The viability rating is Low for primary liquidity and Low-Medium as an auxiliary receivables-collection gateway, subject to Swiss AML outsourcing rules and FINMA guidance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is generally expected for non-resident, politically exposed, or enhanced-risk corporate clients, particularly a pure holding SPV with intermediate ownership layers. Remote account opening is permitted under Swiss law when the bank uses a FINMA-approved electronic identification procedure satisfying the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance, and FINMA Circular 2016/07 on the due diligence of financial intermediaries; however, for first-time director onboarding and for accounts involving controlled foreign distributions, banks commonly require a notarised certificate of incumbency, a legalised board resolution, and a virtual or physical interview with each relationship signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or director resident outside Switzerland without verifiable source-of-funds documentation in a jurisdiction perceived as tax-unmatched or high-risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, government-issued address proof, notarised source-of-wealth declaration, audited financial statements of the shareholder, published group organigram, and bank references issued by the foreign parent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intra-group financing arrangements or intercompany debt without an arm's-length fee and contractual substance, creating a restructuring or money-laundering flag for cross-border wire flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany loan agreement, transfer-pricing documentation, board approvals, committee minutes, cash-flow budgets, debtor-side audited statements, and a written confirmation from a licensed tax advisor that financing has an economic rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose of a passive equity-holding SPV already licensed as ISIC 6420, often flagged as a shell or conduit of unexplained incoming dividends or loan repayments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group holding chartee with ultimate parent entity details, business rationale memo, director CVs, list of underlying subsidiaries, shareholder register, share-transfer history, and evidence that no employee-less nominee shell structure is being used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity and share premium contributions must be routed through a licensed Swiss bank by SWIFT wire, usually MT103, using a clear purpose code and remittance field—for capital injections the recommended description is 'Share Capital Increase / Contribution' with reference to the shareholders' resolution; the receiving Swiss bank will require the underlying shareholder loan or equity issuance documents on FINMA request to comply with AMLA article 3, and the economic beneficiary must match the beneficial owner in the KYC dossier. Where the amount exceeds CHF 100,000, the bank must comply with the SNB statistical payment-reporting obligations and, if needed, declare the transaction in customs/statistics under the Swiss trade statistics framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement from the CH-AG must be made by SWIFT MT103 payment orders or by documentary letters of credit issued under SWIFT MT700/MT710 with UCP600 rules; for CHF-denominated domestic transfers, the settlement rail is SIX SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing); for EUR and other key currencies, market counterparties will clear via either the issuing bank's corresponding network, TARGET2 through a euro-area correspondent, or SWIFT-completed nostro transfers; all trade disbursements must be supported by underlying invoices, packing lists, and transport documents to avoid AML and compliance rejection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transactions through licensed Swiss or foreign bank counterparties
Outright foreign exchange forward contracts (delivered) with maturity ≤ 12 months for trade-related cash-flow hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-CHF currencies when actual counterparty settlement is prohibited; CHF is fully convertible so NDFs are only used for exotic currency tails
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS/CCIRS) for matching asset and liability currencies
Currency options purchased for premium protection on anticipated dividend repatriation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts, board report, audit or review report, and profit appropriation resolution approved at the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory records at registered office; not filed with the Swiss Commercial Register for an unlisted holding AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date; the articles of incorporation may extend the general meeting period to twelve months (Art. 699 para. 3 and Art. 958f OR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may incur civil liability for damage caused by non-compliance; shareholders may compel convening of the meeting by court order; no automatic strike-off for this omission alone

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct federal tax return, cantonal and municipal corporate income tax return, and capital tax return, including financial statements, participation schedule and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office as assessment authority, with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for the direct federal tax component
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 31 March following the calendar or permitted business year; administrative extension to 30 September is available upon written application or under the fiduciary extension calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges, procedural fines, default assessment and statutory default interest; prolonged non-cooperation may result in tax enforcement and, ultimately, administrative strike-off proceedings after repeated official notices

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax is 8.5% on taxable net profit; because the federal tax is deductible in computing its own base, the effective federal rate is approximately 7.83%. Cantonal and communal profit taxes are added, producing combined nominal headline rates of approximately 11.9% in Zug, approximately 15%-17% in most business cantons, and approximately 21.1% in Zurich.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: qualifying dividend income and capital gains from equity participations of at least 10% of share capital or a participation market value of at least CHF 1 million, held for 12 months, are exempt from federal and cantonal/communal profit tax. A 10% security margin of the exempt participation income plus a corresponding portion of non-deductible financing costs remains taxable by way of anti-allocation safeguard. No statutory tax holidays are available to a pure equity-holding AG.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form B: Swiss corporate tax return for legal entities, accepted by the cantonal tax administration and transmitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration; filed electronically through the applicable cantonal e-filing portal or the SwissTax/OCI-compatible tax software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, together with provisional tax payments usually calculated on the basis of the prior assessment period
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed within 6 months from the financial year-end; for calendar-year companies the ordinary deadline is 30 June of the following year, with short extensions commonly granted upon written application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, registered office, company register number, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft, AG), tax identification/UID number, principal purpose and reference to ISIC/NACE business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Swiss holding AG, disclose all direct and indirect shareholders, their country of tax residence, and the beneficial owner of each cash-generating participation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet per commercial accounting: share capital, capital reserves, retained earnings, shareholder loans, book value of subsidiaries, third-party debt, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate passive equity participations and shareholder-issued financing instruments; provide an independent valuation of participations when claiming the participation exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement: gross dividend income, interest income, realized capital gains, brokerage and financing expenses, management fees, foreign tax credit claims, and net taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report each dividend line separately by subsidiary and attach the benefit/country ownership chain to prove 10% participation entitlement and the minimum 12-month holding period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments and recalculations: non-deductible expenses, hidden profit distributions, participation exemption deduction, interest expensing adjustments, treaty and unilateral measure adjustments, and after-tax federal tax addition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain contemporaneous board minutes, transfer pricing calculations, and substance evidence in Switzerland; the taxing officer will scrutinize shareholder loans and management charges for constructive dividend risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding and anticipatory tax declaration: declaration of dividends actually paid, taxable reserves distributed, and payment of Swiss anticipatory tax at 35%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no dividend distribution was made in the fiscal year, state 'no distribution'; distribute dividends only after calculating 35% anticipatory tax liquidity and treaty refund rights for the foreign shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signatures: place, date, signatures of the chairman/CEO and a director with accounting supervision authority, and confirmation of completeness and accuracy.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss-resident director or authorised Swiss representative must countersign; non-resident directors are accepted, but the company must retain a Swiss address and at least one Swiss-resident filing agent for service of process.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers procedural penalty charges (Säumniszuschläge) of typically 0.5%-3% of the assessed tax per commenced month, plus default interest at 5% per annum. Continued failure to file leads to official assessment by estimate with a penalty surcharge of up to 30% and can escalate to administrative tax evasion fines of up to the amount of the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) is withheld on distributions of dividends and similar profit distributions made by a Swiss AG; the distributing Swiss company is the statutory debtor and must remit the tax to the Federal Tax Administration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder relying on a Swiss double tax treaty must obtain a certificate of residence (TRC) from its fiscal authority, then file the Federal Tax Administration's treaty relief claim form (including proof of beneficial ownership, share ownership percentage, and holding period), either at source by instructing the Swiss paying agent or by refund application to the FTA within the statutory three-year period from the date of payment. Relief is generally granted as a full or partial refund of the 35% anticipatory tax, to the rate allowed by the applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Switzerland does not impose any statutory withholding tax on outbound royalty payments. Interest: anticipatory tax applies only to taxable interest on Swiss bond-type instruments and money-market instruments, not to ordinary commercial or shareholder loan interest; treaty rates on such taxable debt interest generally range from 0% to 10%, with anti-abuse recharacterization possible for excessive or non-arm's-length interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland does not prescribe statutory minimum thresholds for Master File/Local File, but the Federal Tax Administration expects contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation when the consolidated group turnover exceeds CHF 80 million and aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed CHF 8 million annually; a pure holding SPV with only passive dividend flows should nevertheless keep participations, financing agreements, and arm's-length pricing evidence proportionate to its functions, assets, and risks.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no statutory Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) comparable to Cayman Islands law, but the Swiss tax authorities apply OECD-aligned substance-over-form principles, abuse-of-law doctrines, and treaty anti-abuse rules. A pure equity-holding SPV must maintain real and proportionate economic substance in Switzerland: strategically involved Swiss-resident directors, adopted board minutes actually controlling participation rights, a maintained Swiss registered office, a local Swiss bank account, and sufficient physical or administrative infrastructure to make the owning presence credible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully presenting falsified balance sheets, fabricated subsidiary values, hidden bank accounts, or fictitious expense records to the Swiss tax administration for purposes of reducing federal or cantonal taxation (tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG, and equivalent cantonal tax law).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to three times the tax evaded, imprisonment in aggravated cases, forfeiture of the improperly obtained fiscal benefit, plus full reassessment, penalty interest, and exclusion from amnesty or voluntary disclosure relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors, signatories, and de facto managers can be criminally prosecuted; the company may recover damages through liability suits, but the State can attach personal assets, impose travel bans to guarantee the criminal/procedural process, and order civil restitution against directors acting in wilful breach of duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating profit by omitting dividend income, claiming unfounded participation exemption, or failing to disclose related-party transactions despite the absence of an intent bordering on fraud; simple tax evasion under Art. 175 DBG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine determined with reference to evaded tax, generally up to the amount of the tax evaded, plus 5% default interest and possible 30% assessment surcharge for non-filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who remain passive after knowing of incomplete records may be held jointly liable; personal liability extends to the penalty, the additional tax, and restitution if the company is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing a dividend to a non-resident shareholder without collecting and remitting the 35% anticipatory tax, or disguising distributions as loan repayments to avoid the tax charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss AG remains liable for the unremitted 35% anticipatory tax, plus default interest at 5% per annum and any assessed penalty; interest and penalty amounts are not deductible for profit tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the company is insolvent or being liquidated, the Federal Tax Administration can pursue directors who were responsible for remitting withholding taxes; director liability includes personal civil restitution, travel restrictions, and criminal sanction if the default was wilful.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Company / Lack of Economic Substance / DTA Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a pure equity-holding Swiss AG as a letter-box conduit: no Swiss office, no Swiss-resident director with genuine decision-making power, no local substance, and treaty benefits claimed purely to channel dividends from operating subsidiaries to a foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, refusal of the participation exemption, reclassification of income streams into constructive dividends subject to 35% anticipatory tax, retroactive reassessment, fines for tax evasion, and possible countermeasures under Swiss unilateral international tax measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing tax returns while knowing the company lacks substance are exposed to personal penalties, civil damages to the tax authority, and criminal prosecution for aiding tax fraud; the corporate veil may be pierced so the ultimate foreign shareholder bears the Swiss tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length financing interest or management fees against the Swiss holding entity, repatriating profit via excessive deductible payments, or failing to document the equity holding SPV's actual financing activities and creditworthiness.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment, disallowance of excessive interest/expenses, recharacterization of the excess as a hidden dividend distribution subject to 35% anticipatory tax, additional tax assessment, default interest, and penalty fines up to 100% of the recharacterized amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers approving fraudulent or negligent pricing may be personally sued for damages under the Swiss Code of Obligations; criminal liability arises where pricing documents were fabricated or where the director knowingly aided in tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss holding SPV as a shell to receive and distribute payments on behalf of undisclosed third parties, laundering proceeds of foreign predicate offences, or misleading Swiss banks about the beneficial ownership of structured equity participations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under Art. 305bis (money laundering) of up to three years' imprisonment, or five years for aggravated offences; corporate fines of up to CHF 5 million; freezing and confiscation of assets; regulatory measures by FINMA against involved Swiss financial intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners knowingly participating in laundering face imprisonment, travel bans, and asset seizure; the courts may disregard the corporate form entirely, impose civil restitution, and permanently bar the director from holding Swiss corporate office.
